rationale: The hypothesis posits that Spinocerebellar ataxia 52 (SCA52) caused by heterozygous RAB3A variants presents in nearly all individuals with early-onset gait and limb ataxia and infantile muscular hypotonia alongside cerebellar atrophy and neurodevelopmental delay. While cerebellar ataxia, cerebellar atrophy on neuroimaging, and variable neurodevelopmental features are supported by the primary literature identifying RAB3A mutations in SCA52 (Miyamoto et al., 2026), the hypothesis is directly contradicted regarding the onset and consistency of infantile features: affected individuals in the primary reporting families presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms (accompanied by mild spasticity and tremor) rather than early-onset ataxia and obligatory infantile hypotonia. Furthermore, OMIM #621535 notes that the phenotypic spectrum of RAB3A is expanding from cerebellar ataxia to spastic paraplegia, rather than being confined to a uniform infantile-onset congenital syndrome.

evidence.text: The discovery study for SCA52 identified the heterozygous RAB3A c.247C>T (p.Arg83Trp) variant in two families. Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremor, with variable neurodevelopmental features and consistent cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI.

conflicts: Age of onset: The hypothesis posits that early-onset gait and limb ataxia and infantile hypotonia are core features in nearly all individuals, whereas Miyamoto et al. (2026) report that affected individuals in the founding cohorts presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar ataxia.

Obligate infantile neurodevelopmental manifestations: Infant muscular hypotonia and intellectual disability are not universal or core defining features across all cohorts; instead, Miyamoto et al. observed variable neurodevelopmental features alongside adult-onset degenerative cerebellar ataxia and spasticity.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true phenotypic spectrum of heterozygous RAB3A pathogenic variants across the lifespan, and what determines adult-onset ataxia versus early neurodevelopmental phenotypes?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether specific variant domains or modifier alleles lead to adult-onset SCA versus early-onset neurodevelopmental delay will resolve conflicting reports in the medical literature.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of patients with unexplained hereditary spastic paraplegia or adult-onset pure cerebellar ataxia carry pathogenic RAB3A variants?
new_directions.rationale: Given the expansion of RAB3A to spastic paraplegia and mild spastic ataxia, systematic screening in larger ataxia/HSP cohorts is needed to establish precise phenotypic frequencies.
